creative_intent: To generate a premium cinematic product photograph of a Mikage Zenith Greatsword, focusing on a clean matte B4C technical ceramic material read. The object should maintain its industrial engineering aesthetic with straight geometric edges and a full, readable blade silhouette, featuring a restrained deep crimson heated core visible through narrow mechanical vents. The composition will be centered with controlled low-key studio lighting against a plain dark brutalist concrete background, strictly avoiding abstract drift or material misreads.

must_have: readable contour evidence of a greatsword
restrained deep crimson heated core visible through narrow mechanical vents
exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture

composition.framing: centered composition, full blade silhouette readable

core_risks: drift into abstract or texture-only results
incorrect material read (e.g., glossy plastic, plaster, or metal instead of matte B4C ceramic)
background becoming too prominent or distracting
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: lock the object read and prevent abstract drift
preserve material-only scope without losing the manufactured object read
suppress plaster, gypsum, chalk, concrete, carved stone, mineral banding, sedimentary drift
suppress glossy plastic, PVC sheen, toy-like finish
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
success_criteria: clean matte B4C technical ceramic read is dominant
dry, dense, engineered manufactured-object readability is achieved
manufactured object read is preserved without compromise
no forbidden material reads are present
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
direction_summary: Prioritize a clean matte B4C technical ceramic material read for the Mikage Zenith Greatsword, ensuring the object's manufactured form, straight edges, and full silhouette remain clearly readable. Maintain a dark, dense aesthetic for the ceramic, incorporating the crimson core as a detail. Strictly avoid any material misreads or abstract drift, focusing on a premium product photography style with controlled low-key lighting.
